cohort: 22,841 pregnancies among women with migraine and 228,324 matched pregnancies among women without migraine
finding: Pregnant women with migraine had increased risks of pregnancy-associated hypertension, miscarriage, preterm birth, and cesarean delivery, while their offspring experienced higher risks of adverse neonatal and postnatal outcomes, such as intensive care unit admission and hospitalization.
mod_finding: This study found that migraine in pregnancy was associated with an increased prevalence of cesarean delivery.
